0: A fourth/fifth level adventure for D&D 5E
1: The party's attempt to grab a rare afternoon of downtime is interrupted by a frantic sheep equipped with a @UUID[Item.mHpfuRgJMORDMy5l]{Scroll of Speak to Animals} and a fierce determination to get their attention. This is no mere beast, however, but a wizard fallen victim to an embittered apprentice wielding a @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{Wand of True Polymorph}.
2: Transformed assassins are looking to grab themselves a mutton dinner, while the only object capable of restoring his opposable thumbs lies in the hands of his former pupil and current nemesis. Fortunately, the woolly wizard has found new allies he can rely on, right?
3: Can the heroes put an end to @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Ahmed Noke's} transmutational tyranny and restore an innocent wizard to his true form? There's only one way to find out...
4: The main text is divided into several distinct scenes, each covering a location, encounter or major plot point. Other information, enemy stat blocks and notes are highlighted in grey boxes.
5: While it is possible to run the game on the fly, it is recommended that you read the adventure in its entirety before starting to play.
6: Getting the players into this adventure is pretty straightforward. All that is requires is that they be spending a few days in a town or city large enough to host a wizard.
7: If you want to plant seeds in advance, you may wish to introduce the character of @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} through rumours or idle conversation with shopkeepers and innkeepers, who view him with fear and awe.
8: The adventure begins as the party idle away an afternoon. They might be enjoying a drink at a tavern, resting at their base or simply walking down the street without a care in the world. No matter where they are, however, it soon becomes clear that something quite odd is happening.
9: There is a sound of clattering hooves, surprised yelps and a frantic bleating, Before the party can react, a sheep bounds towards them. The beast appears to be a regular sheep in every way—fluffy white coat, black face, curled horns—but it is carrying and elaborate scroll in its mouth.
10: The sheep tries to get close to the most magically-gifted member of the party and waves the scroll at them, letting them take it should they reach for it.
11: A wax seal purports that it is a @UUID[Item.mHpfuRgJMORDMy5l]{Scroll of Speak With Animals (Modified)}. If a character says this out loud—to explain to other party members, for example—the sheep appears to nod and bleat enthusiastically.
12: Should they use the scroll (simply reading it aloud is enough to activate the spell within), all of them hear the sheep's baaing instantly morphs into cultured, elven-accented @language[Common], albeit with a slight hint of a bleat.
13: After establishing that the player can understand what it's saying, the sheep introduces itself as @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Finethir Shinebright}, a wizard in dire need of aid. If the players are willing to listen, he explains that he recognises them as adventurers and that he is in dire need of their aid.
14: Specifically, he wants them to help take back an extremely powerful magical artefact from a dangerous, possibly insane wizard.
15: He will attempt to tell his story, but shortly after he starts the sound of howling fills the air...
16: A loud howling fills the air, accompanied by the sound of angry yells and the occasional scream that seem to be drawing closer and closer.
17: The cause quickly become apparent as a huge Half-Orc swaggers towards you, pushing his way through the crowd without a care for anybody standing in his way. In front of him walk what appear to be large wolves wearing iron collars, while a hulking figure in a dirty brown cloak travels in his wake with footfalls loud enough to be heard over the ruckus.
18: The Half-Orc sets his small eyes on you and strides forward with one hand resting on the hilt ofa greatsword.
19: "That sheep is Master Noke's... he desires to have it back."
20: The Half-Orc, @UUID[Actor.982b0HKzKpFXwuZn]{Guz}, is accompanied by trio of collared @UUID[Actor.wLRNfVUfbkIm1hlB]{Wolves} with strangely intelligent eyes, while the huge figure behind him is actually a polymorphed @UUID[Actor.7hje6MS1x4EXPmFP]{Brown Bear}.
21: He demands that he be given "Master Noke's sheep," which he claimed has escaped, and is of great sent-ee-ment-all value to his master. Any mention of Shinebright's true nature is met with hollow, mirthless laughter.
22: @UUID[Actor.982b0HKzKpFXwuZn]{Guz} is not a bright fellow, but he is very loyal and determined to complete his task. His trackers know that @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} is there, no matter how well the party tries to hide him, and will not take no for an answer.
23: While he prefers violence and intimidation, he is also willing to offer bribes and promises of magical favours if that looks like the best option.
24: If he feels like he's not making progress, @UUID[Actor.982b0HKzKpFXwuZn]{Guz} will simply attack without warning. The @UUID[Actor.wLRNfVUfbkIm1hlB]{wolves} will follow him up, while the cloaked figure will let its hood fall and run into combat with a terrible roar.
25: The exact details of any battle that breaks out will depend on the location. If it takes place in an inn, tables and overturned chairs litter the floor. In a street, you may wish to have &Reference[condition=frightened] passers-by form zones of &Reference[rule=difficultterrain]{difficult terrain}.
26: All of the beasts still have an intelligent human mind contained within them, and act intelligently. @UUID[Actor.982b0HKzKpFXwuZn]{Guz} is happy to charge into the front line and take on any heavy hitters alongside the @UUID[Actor.7hje6MS1x4EXPmFP]{Brown Bear}.
27: Meanwhile the @UUID[Actor.wLRNfVUfbkIm1hlB]{Wolves} will aim to cut round behind the party in a bid to grab @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright}—he uses the statistics of a @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Pony but with INT and WIS scores of 18 and 14 respectively}.
28: They intend to capture @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright}, not kill him. If @UUID[Actor.982b0HKzKpFXwuZn]{Guz} captures him, he and his allies will set off for Noke's home. The party will have to decide if they follow, potentially launching a chase scene.
29: Arrogant, self-obsessed and filled with an inflated sense of his own ego, Finethir Shinebright is one of the people worst suited to be transformed into a sheep. Still, no matter his form the former elven wizard manages to exude an air of fussy, bookish intellectualism.
30: Despite his flaws, however, he is generally good-hearted. Assuming he notices them and it doesn't inconvenience him too much he will try to help others where possible, though he will loudly complain of their inability to grasp concepts as simple as poly-planal transweave theory.
31: Once upon a time the local nobles, merchants and arcanists spoke the name of Finethir Shinebright with respect, awe and grudging admiration. A master of transmutation, he would regularly be called upon to carry out grand tasks such as clearing blocked roads by turning massive boulders into rabbits. Two years as a sheep have taught him very little about humility, but a lot about grass. If he returns to his natural form, Shinebright is a willow-thin high elf with straw-coloured hair and an extremely long nose.
32: Once Noke's goons have been defeated, distracted or otherwise dealt with, @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} pleads with the party. Without their help, he is doomed. Noke still has many guards still working for him and eventually they will find him.
33: If they're feeling mercenary, he reminds the party that in his true form he is a powerful and wealthy wizard and promises great rewards. He is more than willing to commit to deals that he knows he can't actually fulfil.
34: In any case, Shinebright will explain:
35: Until two years ago he owned and worked out of a tower on the outskirts of town. He was a wizard of no small talent, specialising in transmutation magic. His most prized possession—and probably the key to his success—was an incredibly rare @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{Wand of True Polymorph}.
36: One fateful night he ended from his meditative trance to find his apprentice, @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Ahmed Noke}, standing over him, clutching the @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand}. Shinebright demanded to know what the boy was doing, but the only noise he could produce was an angry 'baaaaah'.
37: The wizard became a virtual prisoner in his own garden. He was forced to graze on nothing but grass and buttercups while hungry wolves and other beasts—actually polymorphed guards—looked on.
38: Last night he felt hope for the first time in many months when Noke left his home without closing the door. Shinebright snuck in, made his way to an old bookshelf and stole the @UUID[Item.mHpfuRgJMORDMy5l]{Scroll of Speak to Animals}. He then rushed into town with the scroll clenched between his teeth, and was searching desperately for the aura of magic that would indicate someone able to activate the spell when he found the party.
39: In order to turn back into his original form he needs another dose of @UUID[Item.ObFh25lgcO5NFXIf]{True Polymorph}. Which means he needs access to his old @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand}.
40: His former apprentice still dwells in Shinebright's old home, located just to the south-east of town. He keeps the @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand} on him at all times and only leaves if he absolutely has to.
41: He knows his old home's layout intimately, and is more than happy to describe it in endless detail.
42: A hulking brute of a half-orc, Guz views violence and intimidation as the only sensible methods for achieving his goals. He also assumes that most people feel the same way, and prefers to get his own violence in first.
43: Though to most outside observers he may appear evil, he is incredibly loyal to @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke}—who genuinely doesn't care what a creature looks like on the outside—and owes him unswerving devotion.
44: Guz isn't particularly intelligent and can be easily confused by quick-talking foes, though this usually just makes him angrier.
45: However, he is also fond of trying to use long, complicated words he has picked up from @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke}—though the extent to which he actually understands what they mean is probably up for debate.
46: The path to Noke's Tower cuts off from a main road a few miles out of town, darting off between a gap in the bushes. It is a well-trodden route that soon begins to weave its way between tall oak trees.
47: Anyone who cares to examine the path for tracks will easily see the impression of many feet and paws, with the most fresh sets appearing to match up with the group led by @UUID[Actor.982b0HKzKpFXwuZn]{Guz}.
48: The track continues through sparse woodland for perhaps a mile without any sign of habitation. Unless they know what to look for, the party may be somewhat surprised by the view that awaits them when Shinebright's old house appears through the treetops.
49: Rather than stone or glass, the house before you seems to have been formed from the living branches of four sturdy oak trees. These have been shaped and woven to create three thick platforms.
50: The lowest of these platforms is roughly 40ft across and sits about 10ft from the ground. The only obvious route up is a gentle slope formed of roots and branches that connects roughly with the main path.
51: Branches curl around its base, creating a rough bowl shape around it. From where you stand it's possible to see flowers and small trees growing around its edge.
52: By far the largest of the three platforms is the middle one, which looks to be around 60ft across. It is about 20ft above the ground and is fully enclosed with a wall formed from twisting branches. You can see evenly spaced, window-sized gaps, as well as what appears to be a door at the point closest to the garden platform.
53: The final, tallest platform is roughly 30ft above the ground, and is much smaller than the others. It looks to be linked to the central platform by another small slope.
54: Scattered beneath the platforms are two small wooden huts and a large outhouse.
55: Noke once hero-worshipped @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} and served as his apprentice for many years. However, as time dragged on and on there was never any change in their relationship.
56: Decades passed and still the master transmuter treated him like a child, expected to cook, clean and recite answers by rote. When Noke pressed him on it, @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} would explain that his was how he had been taught, and didn't seem to register Noke's claims that, as a human, he couldn't spare a century to serve out an apprenticeship.
57: At the same time, Noke began to realise that much of Shinebright's acclaim came not from his own abilities—extensive as they were—but from the @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{Wand of True Polymorph} he wielded.
58: Eventually he cracked, and turned on his former master before setting himself up as a master wizard. However, a combination of guilt and suddenly unstoppered ambition spelled bad news for his mental state.
59: He is paranoid that someone will attack him as he attacked @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} and rarely sleeps. This paranoia has led him to invest in a troop of guards, many of whom he has transmuted into stronger, more bestial forms.
60: When the party arrives at the compound, there is a trio of @UUID[Actor.WbFmf5b1EaoiwwiC]{Apes} either sleeping or playing with an oversized pair of dice on the lawn, with iron @UUID[Item.0XYnFW9OGQUWk6Xk]{greatswords} stuck into the ground next to them. A @UUID[Actor.dIRrSHYc5N9CRaYA]{Brown Bear} is in the outhouse, taking care of business.
61: The door to the central platform is almost always locked, requiring a [[/save ability=str dc=14]] (&Reference[skill=Athletics]) to break down or a DC 12 @UUID[Item.xNyUB3fPpdKnsUsR]{Thieves' Tools} check to pick. Inside, the area is divided up in to three sections. One contains a combination library and lab, one a sitting room and one dining room/kitchen. Untidy bookshelves line much of the outer walls and worktables are covered with stacks of ink-spattered notes and complicated anatomical diagrams of various beasts and monsters.
62: The tallest platform functions as a bedroom for @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke}, containing little beyond a wardrobe, a large wooden bed and a cluttered dressing table.
63: The huts contain one or two beds each, a few of which are oversized, as well as the general detritus of the common men who occupy them.
64: No@UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke}ke is in the central platform, working furiously on new spells. If he notices the party as they approach he will order them to "return the sheep—in return I will not destroy you all."
65: If they talk, he will reveal his reasons for hating @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} and boast disjointedly of his own achievements. He will also ask if they killed 'my man, Guz,' and be visibly upset if they have. Should they refuse to return @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} he will order his men to attack.
66: The most important part of any fight that breaks out is @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke}, who is offensively weak but can buff his allies dramatically. Once the @UUID[Actor.dIRrSHYc5N9CRaYA]{Brown Bear} emerges from the outhouse he will cast @UUID[Item.RBhEcqTGyscg1fR9]{Enlarge/Reduce} on it to increase its damage. He will supplement his minions''' attacks with @UUID[Item.l8CiF0ToQvekPrLh]{Ray of Frost} but will focus on keeping up @status[concentration].
67: The @UUID[Actor.WbFmf5b1EaoiwwiC]{Apes} will act intelligently, and as they are wielding @UUID[Item.0XYnFW9OGQUWk6Xk]{greatswords} their Fist attack is replaced by a Slash that deals 10 ([[/damage 2d6 + 3 type=slashing]]) damage. They aren't likely to fight to the death and will flee once they fall below half health.
68: Once it is clear that the fight is lost, or a player simply gets too close to him, @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} will cast @UUID[Item.ZLcygUhqLwpmEzze]{Expeditious Retreat} and flee into the central platform, locking the door behind him. He will move to his bedroom as fast as he can and casts @UUID[Item.ObFh25lgcO5NFXIf]{True Polymorph} on the largest thing he can find—his bed.
69: Three rounds after he runs away he bursts from the roof of his bedroom riding the @UUID[Actor.Cn5vrOtxjcKT2msw]{Bed Dragon Wyrmling}, a beast that looks like a dragon carved from wood, with billowing bedsheets for wings and a tail that ends in a soft pillow. If the party are in the main living area he will crash through the ceiling and attack.
70: The Wyrmling is not that smart and will use its Splinter Breath as often as possible, simply trying to attack the closest target when it is not available. It will, however, prioritise enemies that use fire against it. While riding the Wyrmling, @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} will simply use @UUID[Item.l8CiF0ToQvekPrLh]{Ray of Frost} to slow down any party members trying to retreat.
71: Should the Wyrmling be lost–either to damage or because @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} loses @status[concentration]–it will turn back into a thoroughly beaten-up old bed. Desperate and unwilling to let his old master win, a babbling @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} will then attempt to use the @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand} on himself, intending to transmute his form into that of some monstrous creature.
72: However, the over-used @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand} will crackle, fizz and malfunction with a loud bang, turning @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} into a @UUID[Actor.jMX5050TXSOGrDOW]{Gibbering Mouther}—a misshapen pile of flesh that bellows incoherently from dozens of mouths. The sad creature will attack mindlessly until completely destroyed.
73: @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} is naturally paranoid and Shinebright's recent escape hasn't exactly improved his outlook. This makes luring him away from the safety of his tower an extremely difficult task, though not an impossible one.
74: Noke's lust for fame and power slightly outweighs his fear of being unseated, for the time being at least. This means that a very, very skilled set of liars with a sufficiently devious plan and a good helping of luck may be able to tempt him with the offer of a particularly prestigious, lucrative contract.
75: Even so, when @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} leaves he will take all of his remaining bodyguards with him and will be extremely quick to suspect the party of betrayal if there is any hint of a double-cross.
76: He will, of course, have his @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand} to hand at all times. Should he be given enough time to cast it, @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} will use a charge of @UUID[Item.ObFh25lgcO5NFXIf]{True Polymorph} to transmute some nearby item into a Wyrmling that uses roughly the same stats as the @UUID[Actor.Cn5vrOtxjcKT2msw]{Bed Dragon Wyrmling}. Depending on what it was made from, it may not have the same flavour and might need to have its resistances/vulnerabilities tweaked slightly.
77: Should the players recover the @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand} it becomes immediately obvious that it is damaged. Anyone proficient in &Reference[skill=Arcana] can tell that it has been modified so it can be used more often, but overuse has rendered it extremely unreliable.
78: If they wish to speak to @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright}, a quick search of the central platform will allow them to find another @UUID[Item.mHpfuRgJMORDMy5l]{Scroll of Speak with Animals}. At the sight of his former apprentice's ruined corpse, @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} may even undergo some realisation of how poorly he treated his former apprentice and turn somber despite his triumph.
79: Even if he is made aware of the dangers associated with his old @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{wand}, @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} will still be willing to risk his life in order to be turned back into an Elf. However, he is also open to persuasion if the party try to talk him out of it. A compelling argument and a [[/save ability=cha dc=15]] (&Reference[skill=Persuasion]) will be enough to make the former Wizard reconsider his options.
80: Before undergoing the risk of having the spell performed on him, @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} will ask that if he does die, the party send word to his old college.
81: @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} congratulates the party heartily. He will have to be reminded of anything he actually promised them while he was still a sheep, and cannot actually pay any financial reward, as @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} was virtually bankrupt and had sold most items to pay for research materials and guards.
82: He will, however, be willing to perform transmutations of up to 5th level for them, charging just enough to cover the components. He will also take in any polymorphed guards who fled, promising to work towards returning them to their natural shapes.
83: @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} dies permanently. The party is free to honour his final wish and leave the tower more-or-less intact, or loot to their hearts' content. The tower is surprisingly empty of anything of benefit to non-transmuters, however, with valuables restricted to expensive lab equipment and arcane paraphernalia estimated to be worth around 1,000gp. If the players wish they can also take the entire tower complex as their own, though this may cause trouble when the local nobles try to pay @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} a visit and find him missing...
84: @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} accepts but will not give up his hopes entirely. He will take back his old home and work towards a way to remove his curse. In any case, he heads to the bedroom and slips on one of his old robes, which he wears until he is transformed back to his natural shape. Though he will be upset with them, Shinebright will acknowledge that he owes the party a large debt.
85: In any case, any adventurers that help @UUID[Actor.2MW3RWFTmRWjC7K1]{Shinebright} to deal with @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} each receive 500xp.
86: A stealthy party may be able to steal the wand while @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} sleeps or a combination of lucky roles and inventive tactics may allow a player to disarm the wizard.
87: Should this happen, don't force the story back towards the 'ideal path', but allow it to develop naturally.
88: One thing that you must do, however, is try to provide at least a hint of the dangers associated with the @UUID[Item.0jpyem8I92uMoE18]{modified wand} before the players try and use it. Possibly it sparks unnaturally when a character touches it, or @UUID[Actor.R6I8OaPfn3fewtWh]{Noke} himself may feel honour bound to warn them.
